description: A pure CALCULATION node — invert a SQUARE matrix (A⁻¹) by Gauss–Jordan elimination. Matrix in, matrix out; draws nothing. Non-square or singular input → empty.
instructions:
A value-only node: a SQUARE matrix as JSON in, its inverse as JSON out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

INPUT: wire a square matrix into valin-matrix — Grid Geometry's `val-matrix` (a bare n×n 2D array `[[…],…]`), or another Matrix node's output (e.g. AᵀA from Transpose → Multiply). A val-grid `{ "values": [[…]] }` is accepted too.

METHOD: Gauss–Jordan elimination with partial pivoting. A non-square matrix, or a singular one (pivot ≈ 0), returns an EMPTY matrix — check `val-rows` > 0. Note: inverting AᵀA is the textbook least-squares step but numerically shaky for large / ill-conditioned systems (a QR-based Least Squares node is the robust alternative).

OUTPUT: `val-matrix` — the inverse; plus `val-rows` / `val-cols`. Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
